Theorem
[Consistency of viscosity solutions] ↗ def:viscosity-solution-cauchy-problem ↗ lem:touching-by-c1-function 1. ch10:10.1-thm-1\group Viscosity Solutions

Let $u$ be a viscosity solution of (1), and suppose $u$ is differentiable at some point $(x_0, t_0) \in \R ^n \times (0, \infty )$. Then \[ u_t(x_0, t_0) + H(Du(x_0, t_0), x_0) = 0. \]

Proof

\sketch The touching lemma in space-time supplies a $C^1$ function touching $u$ strictly from above at the differentiability point. Mollify it; nearby maxima converge to the contact point, so the viscosity subsolution inequality passes to the limit and gives the PDE inequality $\leq 0$. Apply the same argument to $-u$ for the reverse inequality.

□
